exact_reference: Mafātīḥ al-ghayb, Vol. 2, p. 261 (Commentary on 2:2)
original_quote: كَأَنَّ الْعَبْدَ لَمَّا قَالَ: {اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ} قِيلَ لَهُ: قَدْ سَأَلْتَ الْهِدَايَةَ، فَهَاكَ الْكِتَابَ الَّذِي فِيهِ تِلْكَ الْهِدَايَةُ، وَهُوَ: {ذَلِكَ الْكِتَابُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ هُدًى لِلْمُتَّقِينَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: It is as though when the servant said: 'Guide us to the straight path', it was answered to him: 'You have asked for guidance; take then this Book in which is that very guidance: That is the Book about which there is no doubt, guidance for those conscious of Allah.'

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar fī tanāsub al-āyāt wa al-suwar, Vol. 1, p. 35
original_quote: فَكَانَ افْتِتَاحُ سُورَةِ الْبَقَرَةِ نَفْسَ مَا انْتَهَتْ إِلَيْهِ الْفَاتِحَةُ، لِأَنَّ خَاتِمَةَ الْفَاتِحَةِ دُعَاءٌ بِالْهِدَايَةِ إِلَى الصِّرَاطِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ، وَأَوَّلُ الْبَقَرَةِ بَيَانُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ الصِّرَاطَ الْمَطْلُوبَ هُوَ هَذَا الْكِتَابُ الَّذِي لَا شَكَّ فِيهِ.
translation_or_paraphrase: The opening of Surah Al-Baqarah is the very destination at which Al-Fatihah concluded, because the conclusion of Al-Fatihah is a supplication for guidance to the straight path, and the beginning of Al-Baqarah is the clarification that the sought-after path is this Book in which there is no doubt.

exact_reference: Al-Burhān fī tartīb suwar al-Qur'ān, Ed. Shaʿbānī, pp. 177-182
original_quote: ولما اشتملت أم الكتاب على الإجمال الذي وقع تفصيله في باقي القرآن... افتتحت البقرة بما يعين على سلوك هذا الصراط المستقيم.
translation_or_paraphrase: Since the Mother of the Book contains the concise summation whose detailed exposition occurs in the remainder of the Qur'an... Al-Baqarah opened with that which aids in traversing this straight path.

exact_reference: Tanāsuq al-durar fī tanāsub al-suwar, Ed. ʿAṭā, p. 65
original_quote: افتتحت سورة البقرة بالدلالة على أن هذا الكتاب هو الهداية المطلوبة في قوله: {اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: Surah Al-Baqarah opened with the indication that this Book is the guidance requested in His saying: 'Guide us to the straight path.'

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar, Vol. 1, pp. 38-42
original_quote: فصلت سورة البقرة أصناف الخلق الثلاثة الذين أجملتهم الفاتحة: المتقين، والكافرين، والمنافقين.
translation_or_paraphrase: Surah Al-Baqarah details the three classes of creation that Al-Fatihah summarized: the Muttaqun (the favored), the Kafiroon (those who incurred wrath), and the Munafiqoon (those astray).

exact_reference: Al-Burhān fī tartīb suwar al-Qur'ān, p. 180
original_quote: بيّن سبحانه في صدر البقرة أحوال الفرق الثلاث المذكورة في ختام الفاتحة أتم بيان.
translation_or_paraphrase: He, the Exalted, explained in the beginning of Al-Baqarah the states of the three groups mentioned at the conclusion of Al-Fatihah in the most complete clarification.

exact_reference: Al-Taḥrīr wa al-tanwīr, Vol. 3, pp. 138-142
original_quote: جاء ختام سورة البقرة مناجياً متضرعاً كما كان شأن الفاتحة، فتلاقت خاتمتها مع فاتحتها وفاتحة الكتاب.
translation_or_paraphrase: The conclusion of Surah Al-Baqarah arrived in intimate supplication and humble petition, just as was the condition of Al-Fatihah; thus its ending harmonizes with its own opening and the opening of the Scripture.

exact_reference: Al-Burhān fī tartīb suwar al-Qur'ān, Ed. Shaʿbānī, pp. 312-315
original_quote: لَمَّا خَتَمَ الْقَمَرَ بِقَوْلِهِ: {فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكٍ مُّقْتَدِرٍ}، افْتَتَحَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِتَعْرِيفِ ذَلِكَ الْمَلِيكِ فَقَالَ: {الرَّحْمَٰنُ}، ثُمَّ لَمَّا كَرَّرَ فِي الْقَمَرِ: {وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ}، بَيَّنَ فِي الرَّحْمَنِ أَنَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ الَّذِي يَسَّرَهُ فَقَالَ: {عَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: When He concluded Al-Qamar with His saying: 'In a seat of honor near an Omnipotent Sovereign' [54:55], He opened Ar-Rahman by defining that Sovereign, saying: 'The Most Merciful' [55:1]. Furthermore, when He repeated four times in Al-Qamar: 'And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance', He clarified in Ar-Rahman that He is the One who facilitated it, saying: 'Taught the Quran' [55:2].

exact_reference: Tanāsuq al-durar fī tanāsub al-suwar, Ed. ʿAṭā, p. 132
original_quote: خاتمة القمر في بيان جزاء المتقين عند مليك مقتدر، وفاتحة الرحمن سمّت ذلك المليك وأفاضت في آلائه ونعمه.
translation_or_paraphrase: The conclusion of Al-Qamar clarifies the recompense of the righteous near an Omnipotent Sovereign, and the opening of Ar-Rahman named that Sovereign and expanded upon His bounties and favors.

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar, Vol. 19, pp. 110-115
original_quote: الجنتان الأوليان في الرحمن للسابقين المقربين، والجنتان الأخريان لأصحاب اليمين، وقد فصّلت الواقعة أحوال هذين الصنفين وأحوال أصحاب الشمال.
translation_or_paraphrase: The two initial gardens in Ar-Rahman belong to the Foremost who are brought near, and the two subsequent gardens belong to the Companions of the Right, and Al-Waqi'ah detailed the conditions of these two categories along with the Companions of the Left.

exact_reference: Tanāsuq al-durar, Ed. ʿAṭā, p. 134
original_quote: أمر في آخر الواقعة بالتسبيح فقال: {فَسَبِّحْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الْعَظِيمِ}، وأخبر في أول الحديد بوقوع التسبيح من جميع الكائنات فقال: {سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: He commanded tasbih at the end of Al-Waqi'ah, saying: 'So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great', and informed at the beginning of Al-Hadid of the occurrence of tasbih by all beings, saying: 'Whatever is in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah.'

exact_reference: Al-Burhān fī tartīb suwar al-Qur'ān, Ed. Shaʿbānī, pp. 183-185
original_quote: لما ختمت سورة البقرة بالدعاء بالنصر على القوم الكافرين في قوله: {فَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ}، افتتحت آل عمران ببيان من يُستنصر به وهو {اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ}، ثم أتبع ذلك بإنذار الكافرين بأنهم سيُغلبون في قوله: {قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَتُغْلَبُونَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: When Surah Al-Baqarah concluded with the supplication for victory over the disbelieving people [2:286], Al 'Imran opened by identifying the One from Whom alone victory is sought — 'Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence' [3:2] — followed by warning the disbelievers that they will surely be overcome [3:12].

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar fī tanāsub al-āyāt wa al-suwar, Vol. 2, pp. 5-10
original_quote: سورة البقرة لأصل الدين وتأسيس قواعده، وسورة آل عمران للدفاع عنه والرد على من خالفه من أهل الكتاب.
translation_or_paraphrase: Surah Al-Baqarah is for establishing the foundation of the religion and instituting its rules, while Surah Al 'Imran is for defending it and refuting those from the People of the Book who oppose it.

exact_reference: Tanāsuq al-durar, Ed. ʿAṭā, p. 70
original_quote: لما قرر في البقرة أن الكتاب لا ريب فيه، بيّن في آل عمران انقسامه إلى محكم ومتشابه.
translation_or_paraphrase: When it was established in Al-Baqarah that the Book contains no doubt, it was clarified in Al 'Imran its division into clear, decisive verses and allegorical verses.

exact_reference: Al-Taḥrīr wa al-tanwīr, Vol. 3, pp. 154-159
original_quote: جاءت آية المحكم والمتشابه قاعدة منهجية كبرى لحماية الأمة من التفرق والتأويل الباطل.
translation_or_paraphrase: The verse of the clear and ambiguous was revealed as a major methodological foundation to protect the Ummah from division and false interpretation.

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar, Vol. 2, pp. 11-15
original_quote: استوفت البقرة مجادلة اليهود، واستوفت آل عمران مجادلة النصارى.
translation_or_paraphrase: Al-Baqarah exhaustively addressed the disputation with the Jews, and Al 'Imran exhaustively addressed the disputation with the Christians.

exact_reference: Marāṣid al-maṭāliʿ fī tanāsub al-maqāṭiʿ wa al-maṭāliʿ, p. 45
original_quote: انْظُرْ إِلَى حُسْنِ هَذَا التَّنَاسُبِ: افْتَتَحَ السُّورَةَ بِإِثْبَاتِ الْفَلَاحِ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَخَتَمَهَا بِنَفْيِ الْفَلَاحِ عَنِ الْكَافِرِينَ، فَكَانَ آخِرُهَا مُلَاحِماً لِأَوَّلِهَا تَمَامَ الِالْتِحَامِ.
translation_or_paraphrase: Look at the beauty of this harmony: He opened the surah by affirming success for the believers, and closed it by negating success from the disbelievers; thus its ending was completely welded to its beginning.

exact_reference: Al-Burhān fī ʿulūm al-Qur'ān, Type 35, Vol. 1, p. 38
original_quote: ومن بديع التناسب مقابلة الفاتحة بالخاتمة كقوله في المؤمنون: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ} وختمها بقوله: {إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الْكَافِرُونَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: And of exquisite harmony is contrasting the opening with the conclusion, as in His saying in Al-Mu'minun: 'Certainly will the believers succeed' and closing it with His saying: 'Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.'

exact_reference: Naẓm al-durar, Vol. 14, pp. 380-385
original_quote: لما ذكر في أولها قصة موسى وخروجه خائفاً ثم عودته منصوراً، بشّر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في آخرها بالعودة إلى بلده ومكة داره.
translation_or_paraphrase: When He mentioned in its beginning the story of Moses and his departure in fear followed by his victorious return, He gave glad tidings to the Prophet at its end of returning to his land and home of Mecca.

exact_reference: Mafātīḥ al-ghayb, Vol. 25, p. 19
original_quote: قوله لموسى في أول السورة: {رَبِّ بِمَا أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ فَلَنْ أَكُونَ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ} طابق قوله للنبي في آخرها: {فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ ظَهِيرًا لِّلْكَافِرِينَ}.
translation_or_paraphrase: His words regarding Moses in the beginning of the surah: 'My Lord, for the favor You bestowed upon me, I will never be an assistant to the criminals' matches His words to the Prophet at its end: 'So do not be an assistant to the disbelievers.'
